description: Publish a local app or a URL as a private qURL resource with the qURL CLI on this machine, and return its CRID. No account is needed. For a local app pass its loopback address, such as http://127.0.0.1:3000; the CLI starts its background service, waits until the app is served, and the share then survives sleep and restarts. The resource is private: only this machine and the people the publisher allows can open it; there is no public option. Always supply app_name: use the user’s app name or choose a short neutral one. This name is public; keep secrets and recipient details out. The tool sets and checks it before returning success. Include app_name and resource_url in your answer even when invitation emails are sent. Publishing the same target again returns the same CRID (found_existing true); never delete and republish to refresh. Passing policy or allow_requests for an existing target changes its policy and requires the user to authorize that change. For legacy resources without consumer_access, allow_requests lets people ask at resource_url and give the publisher a six-digit code; approve it with manage_crid_requests. Use share_by_crid only for legacy resources without consumer_access. For consumer_access policies, use resource_url and the policy's invitation or grant flow. Publishing does not close other routes to the app. Confirm with the user before publishing a remote URL on their behalf.

alias.description: Memorable handle stored with a remote URL resource

allow_requests.description: Legacy resources without consumer_access only: let people ask for access from a browser. Each asker gets a six-digit code to give the publisher, who approves it with manage_crid_requests. Also turns requests on for a target that is already published privately.

app_name.description: Public app name shown before access. Always provide a short name; use the requested name or choose a neutral one. Keep secrets and recipient details out.

description.description: Description stored with a remote URL resource

policy.description: Optional initial private access policy (see manage_crid_access). Cannot be combined with allow_requests. contract_id is required only for contract mode.

target_url.description: What to publish: a local app as http://127.0.0.1:PORT, http://localhost:PORT, or http://[::1]:PORT (no path), or a remote http(s) URL. A local app must already be running.

name: publish_crid

crid.description: The resource's permanent ID. Safe to share; grants no access by itself

name.description: Self-declared publisher name; not proof of identity

resource_id.description: Equals a valid crid when present; otherwise a legacy publisher key that management tools do not accept.

resource_url.description: Permanent browser address. Include it in your answer, including for invitation-only shares; recipients still need their emailed invitation.

title: Publish a private CRID
